checked.comment: Stochastic K-armed bandit with rewards in [0,1], pseudo-regret; matches the paper. KL-MS takes only K as input.
Same setting, but the learner also knows T, because KL-UCB++ uses T and K in its exploration function.
Theorem 1 is transcribed faithfully: constants 392, c^2, the kl arguments and the Min/Max inside the log are all correct. The restriction to Delta_i > Delta is recorded in the regime.
Theorem 3 matches: sqrt(dmu_1 K T ln K) + K ln T.
Theorem 4 is a limsup upper bound with kl(mu_a, mu_1). The note on '=' vs '<=' is appropriate.
Matches the first display of Theorem 30. Only the last term is inside O(); this is noted.
Matches the second display of Theorem 30.
Theorem 32 matches: O(sqrt(dmu_1 T K^3 ln T) + K^2 ln T).
Theorem 34 matches. The horizon is somewhat ambiguous, and the note says so.

missing_results.description: Refined bound on the expected number of pulls of a suboptimal arm for KL-UCB++ (a pull-count guarantee, intermediate to Theorem 32).

summary: The extraction is accurate. All eight results match the paper's statements: expressions, constants, notation, horizon and setting are correct, and the algorithm registry ids are correct. The only gap is Theorem 31, an intermediate pull-count bound for KL-UCB++ that was not extracted, which is arguably a technical step rather than a separate guarantee.
